Jordan — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of goals
- Use embeddings-powered semantic search over JordanTech's product KB + engineering notes (~40k docs) to improve dev self-serve and reduce support MTTR.
- Success metrics: recall@10 > 0.85 for canonical Q/A, p@1 > 0.6 for top-1 intent routing, median latency (search + embed) < 50ms for single-query paths.
- Non-functional: plan for incremental re-indexing (daily), drift detection, and cost target under $Xk/month (we'll refine with volume).

What I recommend from the demo & quick audit
- Candidate embedding models: redwood-embedding-small-v1 (256d, low-cost), redwood-embedding-standard-v2 (768d, balance), open-embed-2B (1536d, highest quality for paraphrase-heavy content).
- Quantized variant (redwood-embedding-quantized-v1) is worth testing if cost is a binding constraint; expect slight quality delta in tail cases.
- Indexing: HNSW with faiss for production; test recall/latency tradeoffs at ef/search=128.

Immediate next steps
1) We will run an initial fit-validation run on a 2k doc sample of your KB (we'll use your labeled queries + click data where available).
2) Redwood will produce a short benchmark report (recall@10, MRR, p@1, mean cosine similarity, basic clustering silhouette) and an inference cost estimate per 1M queries.
3) Share prompt sets and evaluation scripts used so results are reproducible.
4) Schedule a 30-min results review next week.

I attached a one-page mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) with owner names and timelines. I'll follow up with the benchmark link and prompt set after we ingest the sample.

If you agree, please reply with the sample subset you'd like us to use (or we can sample randomly from the KB and include a stratified set of recent docs).

Thanks,
Marcus

Jordan — great questions, answers below and I've linked sample artifacts. TL;DR: we'll run recall@10 + MRR as primary, surface p@1 and mean cosine similarity for signal on top-1 quality, and report a small set of clustering metrics to catch semantic collapse.

Metrics & definitions
- Recall@K (primary): fraction of queries where at least one relevant doc is in top-K (we'll use K=10).
- MRR (secondary): mean reciprocal rank across queries (sensitive to top placement).
- p@1: precision at 1 for intent-critical queries.
- Mean cosine similarity: average cosine between query and positive doc embedding (useful as a drift/health metric).
- Silhouette score (sanity check): measure of cluster separability on a labeled subset.

Dimensionality trade-offs
- 1536d (open-embed-2B): best for paraphrase-heavy queries; expect ~5-8% lift in recall@10 vs a 256d small model on your dataset based on similar KBs we've tested.
- 768d (redwood-embedding-standard-v2): good middle ground — often within 2-4% of 1536d but at significantly lower compute cost.
- 256d (redwood-embedding-small-v1): strong latency/cost benefits; suitable if budget is constrained or if you apply supervised fine-tuning/contrastive re-ranking downstream.

Cost delta (rough ballpark for 1M queries - inference only)
- redwood-embedding-small-v1 (256d): ~$40–60
- redwood-embedding-standard-v2 (768d): ~$120–180
- open-embed-2B (1536d): ~$300–420

Artifacts & reproducibility
- Benchmark report (preview): s3://redwood-evals/jordantech/initial_benchmarks/20261115/overview.pdf
- Prompt/eval set: prompt_set_v2.csv (attached) — includes labeled queries, negative sampling policy, and 200 holdout queries for manual review.
- Eval script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/tree/main/embeddings

Quality regression concerns
- We'll run paired comparisons (A/B on the same sample) to flag regressions >2% recall@10 delta. If we see regressions after a model/quantization change, recommended mitigations are: 1) narrow candidate model, 2) enable hybrid reranking (lexical + semantic), 3) increase recall candidate window and rerank.

Next: we'll start ingestion on the sample if you confirm the subset. Expect an initial benchmark within 48 hours of receiving the sample.

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Marcus

Jordan — quick technical notes to add on Marcus's excellent summary. Two practical items for the validation run: 

1) Thresholds & drift detection
- We instrument a rolling mean cosine similarity per shard and alert if the 7-day mean drops >0.06 relative to the training sample baseline. That tends to flag topical drift without too many false positives.
- Also track Recall@10 on a small set of daily queries (synthetic probes) for production health.

2) Indexing & dimensionality guidance
- For 1536d vectors: use IVF-PQ or HNSW with product quantization for storage savings; ensure PQ codebooks are trained on a representative sample to avoid quantization artifacts.
- For 256d: much smaller index and faster queries; if recall gap is >5% we recommend a cheap contrastive fine-tune on ~10k in-domain pairs.
- Consider PCA to 256/384 dims for indexing speed if you want to keep 1536d model quality but reduce index cost — re-evaluate MRR after PCA.

We'll also include a short script in the eval bundle to compute these signals and produce a one-page health dashboard. Marcus — I'll drop the script artifact into the shared Drive link.

-Rishi
